retrieved_from: Ported byte-for-byte from Chemclaw3's `src/chemclaw/science/safety/ich_q3c.yaml`, transcribed there by hand from ICH Q3C(R9), 'Impurities: Guideline for Residual Solvents', ICH Step 4 / minor revision, 2024 — Table 1 (Class 1), Table 2 (Class 2), Table 3 (Class 3). Nothing is fetched at runtime and no address here is read by any code.
description: 62 residual solvents with their Q3C class, concentration limit in ppm and — for Classes 2 and 3 — a PDE in mg/day, plus what each class means. THREE RECORDED CAVEATS TRAVEL WITH THIS FILE AND MUST NOT BE DROPPED. (1) The revision label 'R9 / 2024' is the one field nobody has verified against the source document, and it appears in every row's citation — an adversarial review verified all 62 values and could not verify this, so if the label is wrong the whole file cites the wrong document while every number in it is right. (2) tert-Butyl alcohol is DELIBERATELY OMITTED: Q3C(R8) assigns it a PDE the transcriber could not verify, and a miss that says 'read the guideline' is honest where a guessed PDE is not. Water is absent because Q3C does not cover it. (3) The ambiguous abbreviations EDC, DMA and TCE are deliberately not synonyms of anything here, because a confidently wrong row arrives with a real citation attached. Class 3's two figures are the guideline's general statement (50 mg/day or more is acceptable without justification), not a solvent-specific assignment, and every Class 3 row is labelled as such. Class 2 rows satisfy the guideline's own ppm = PDE x 100 identity at a 10 g/day dose, which is the internal check `tests/test_dataset.py` runs over the whole table.
